statement: In a contest, a wrong answer costs nothing. Each question has 5 answer choices and is worth 4 points. With one minute left, Ben guesses at random on his last 10 questions. On average, how many points will these guesses earn him?

choices.misconception: I thought random guesses earn nothing, so it is not worth answering.
I found how many questions he gets right on average and gave that instead of the points.
I thought a guess is right one time in ten, so one question right, worth 4 points.
I thought a guess is right half the time, so I gave 5 questions right.

hints: With 5 choices, how often is a random guess right?
A random guess picks the right answer one time in five. Work out how many of the 10 guesses are right on average, then turn that into points, remembering that wrong answers lose nothing.
One fifth of 10 guesses is 2 right answers on average, and each is worth 4 points.

solutions.reliable: With 5 choices, a random guess is right one time in five. Over 10 guesses that is 10 ÷ 5 = 2 right answers on average. Each is worth 4 points, so the guesses earn 2 × 4 = 8 points on average, and since wrong answers cost nothing there is nothing to subtract. The transferable idea: when there is no penalty for a wrong answer, a guess can only help, so never leave a question blank.

whyOnTest: With no penalty for wrong answers, every blank throws away points; this makes the size of that gift concrete.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
